simple.meaning: דָּקַק (dâqaq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to crush (or intransitively) crumble.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 13 times across Exodus, Deuteronomy, 2 Samuel, 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, and 2 more, beginning at Exodus 30:36. Its contexts include family line, altar, covenant, mountain, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דָּקַק (H1854).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: דָּקַק (dâqaq) / H1854 is traced through Exodus 30:36, Exodus 32:20, Deuteronomy 9:21, 2 Samuel 22:43 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.usage: beat in pieces (small), bruise, make dust, (into) × powder, (be, very) small, stamp (small).

Hiph`il Perfect הֵדַק 2Kin 23:15 ; 2Chr 34:4 ; 2 feminine singular וַהֲדִקּוֺתְ consecutive Micah 4:13 ; Imperfect וַיָּ֫דֶק 2Kin 23:6 ; 2Chr 15:16 ; 1 singular suffix אֲדִקֵּם 2Sam 22:43 (but אֲרִיקֵם || Psa 18:43 ); Infinitive absolute הָדֵק Exod 30:36 ; construct לְהֵדַק 2Chr 34:7 (form anomalous compare Ew § 238 d Ol § 258 b Be; read perhaps לְהָדֵק Ki; or לָדַק [see כַּדַּק Isa 40:15 ] compare Öttli); — make dust of, pulverize לְעָפָר וַיָּ֫דֶק 2Kin 23:6 (i.e. the Ashera), || 2Chr 34:4 , 7 ( לְהֵדַק כִּתַּת ); so of the bamah לְעָפָר הֵדַק 2Kin 23:15 ; of the מִפְלֶצֶת 2Chr 15:16 ; figurative Micah 4:13 (object רַבִּים עַמִּים ); Exod 30:36 (P) has הָדֵק מִמֶּנָּה וְשָׁחַקְתָּ֫ and thou shalt beat some of it fine (i.e. the incense); 2Sam 22:43 read אֲרִיקֵם (|| Psa 18:43 ) for אֲדִקֵּם . occurrences.englishText: You shall beat some of it very small, and put some of it before the covenant in the Tent of Meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be to you most holy.
He took the calf which they had made, and burned it with fire, ground it to powder, and scattered it on the water, and made the children of Israel drink it.

I took your sin, the calf which you had made, and burned it with fire, and crushed it, grinding it very small, until it was as fine as dust. I threw its dust into the brook that descended out of the mountain.
Then I beat them as small as the dust of the earth.

He brought out the Asherah from Yahweh’s house, outside of Jerusalem, to the brook Kidron, and burned it at the brook Kidron, and beat it to dust, and cast its dust on the graves of the common people.

Moreover the altar that was at Bethel, and the high place which Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, had made, even that altar and the high place he broke down; and he burned the high place and beat it to dust, and burned the Asherah.

Also Maacah, the mother of Asa the king, he removed from being queen, because she had made an abominable image for an Asherah; so Asa cut down her image, ground it into dust, and burned it at the brook Kidron.

They broke down the altars of the Baals in his presence; and he cut down the incense altars that were on high above them. He broke the Asherah poles, the engraved images, and the molten images in pieces, made dust of them, and scattered it on the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
He broke down the altars, and beat the Asherah poles and the engraved images into powder, and cut down all the incense altars throughout all the land of Israel, then returned to Jerusalem.
Bread flour must be ground; so he will not always be threshing it. Although he drives the wheel of his threshing cart over it, his horses don’t grind it.

Behold, I have made you into a new sharp threshing instrument with teeth.
Arise and thresh, daughter of Zion;
